prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1168; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving two insured vehicles. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and statements from two witnesses, who both describe the impact in the same way the claimant did. Photos taken at the scene are consistent with that account.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the sequence of events and placed the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision, which police also noted.

Entry 4: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The damage pattern lines up with the impact described, and no older damage was visible in the affected area.

Entry 5: Checked the policy records. The driver involved is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: Received the medical summary showing neck and back strain. The injury type and severity fit the force of the collision as reported.

Entry 7: Attorney provided the treatment records. Care followed a typical course and eased off as the claimant improved, with no unusual gaps or add-on procedures.

Entry 8: The medical history includes a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved completely with no ongoing complaints noted in the records.

Entry 9: Took a recorded follow-up call with the claimant. The account matched what was given at first notice, with the same details repeated without change.

Entry 10: Reviewed the prior-damage check and vehicle history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 11: Based on the police report, witness statements, photos, vehicle inspection, and medical records, the claim is consistent throughout and is moving forward for standard evaluation through counsel.
